annotations.text:
Editing a question

Three columns: steps, the outline, the live patient form.

Selecting a row in the outline expands it INTO an editor in place — no separate inspector panel to look across at — and highlights the same question in the form on the right.

Follow-ups are arranged by ANSWER: "Other → then ask 1 more". The branch also appears in the outline as a real child on a connector line, tagged "if Other", so the logic is readable without opening anything.

A brand-new form

The state he will actually test first: a service with nothing in it.

An empty outline is where a builder feels hardest, so it offers two ways in besides the blank search field — the patient basics every form needs, and copying a step from a service he has already built.

The preview column says plainly that this is the same screen the patient sees, not an approximation. That is the claim Zoho could not make.

Adding a question

The 18 field types were a flat rail of 18 items you had to read top to bottom. Here it is one search field: type a few letters, the best match is first and takes Enter.

Below it the rest are grouped — Choice, Clinical & consent, Text, Numbers — so browsing still works when he does not know what the thing is called.

The hint text is written for a pharmacist, not a developer: "Weight, height or waist — metric or imperial, patient chooses", not "measurement".

Not drawn, deliberately

· Drag-to-reorder is shown by the grip handles, but the drop indicator is behavioural — it will be built, not mocked.
· The "copy a step from another service" flow needs a picker that does not exist yet; the entry point is drawn, the picker is not.
· Publishing already works and is unchanged — this redesign does not touch how versions are created.
